articles.headline: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander scores 40 as Thunder beat Pelicans 126-120 in NBA Cup
articles.description: — Shai Gilgeous-Alexander scored 40 points and the Oklahoma City Thunder rallied in the fourth quarter for a 126-120 win over the New Orleans Pelicans on Friday night to improve to 2-1 in NBA Cup play.
articles.body:
OKLAHOMA CITY -- — Shai Gilgeous-Alexander scored 40 points and the Oklahoma City Thunder rallied in the fourth quarter for a 126-120 win over the New Orleans Pelicans on Friday night to improve to 2-1 in NBA Cup play.


              Gilgeous-Alexander's 3-point play with 34.8 seconds left gave Oklahoma City, which trailed by 16 points in the third quarter, a 124-116 lead. 


              Rookie Aday Mara added 22 points on 11-of-15 shooting and had 16 rebounds for the Thunder. Jared McCain and rookie Bennett Stirtz each scored 18 points for the Thunder, who are 8-5 since the loss of three starters to long-term injuries.


              Zion Williamson and Jeremiah Fears scored 22 points each for New Orleans, which fell to 0-3 in NBA Cup play.


              New Orleans fell behind 11-0 then outscored the Thunder 64-45 to lead 64-56 at halftime. Williamson led the Pelicans with 18 points but picked up his third foul with less than a minute to play when he sent Gilgeous-Alexander to the floor. The two-time league MVP was slow to get up, which quieted the home crowd. He made both free throws to finish the half with 19 points.


              A 3-pointer by Herb Jones, his fourth of the game, gave New Orleans a 91-76 lead with four minutes left in the third quarter. But Oklahoma City responded with a 16-7 run fueled by back-to-back baskets by Stirtz and a 3 by Gilgeous-Alexander to pull to within 98-92 to start the fourth.


              The Thunder pulled even at 102 on a 24-foot shot by McCain with 9:22 remaining and took a 108-102 lead on a basket by Isaiah Hartenstein. 


              Up next
              Pelicans: Play at San Antonio on Saturday night.


              Thunder: Play at Miami on Sunday night.

articles.headline: Franz Wagner scores 35, hits late jumper to lift Magic over Nets 113-111
articles.description: — Franz Wagner scored 35 points, including a game-winning jumper with 2.4 seconds left, and the Orlando Magic beat the Brooklyn Nets 113-111 in an NBA Cup game on Friday night.
articles.body:
NEW YORK -- — Franz Wagner scored 35 points, including a game-winning jumper with 2.4 seconds left, and the Orlando Magic beat the Brooklyn Nets 113-111 in an NBA Cup game on Friday night.


              Facing his older brother and former teammate Mo Wagner for the first time after spending their last five seasons together in Orlando, Franz Wagner stepped back and hit a 14-foot jumper steps away from the Nets bench.


              Brooklyn called a timeout and Julius Randle had a chance to win it but missed a 28-foot 3-pointer.


              Franz Wagner shot 13 for 25 from the field and made 7 of 9 free throw attempts, including a pair in the opening minute of the second quarter when he was fouled by Mo Wagner, who signed with the Nets as a free agent in July after eight seasons in Orlando.


              Desmond Bane finished with 21 points, reserve Nikola Vucevic chipped in 15 points and Anthony Black had 13 for the Magic, who have won five of their last six games.


              Randle scored 27 and Danny Wolf, who started in place of Egor Demin, added 20 points for the Nets, who have lost their last four games.


              Brooklyn fell to 1-6 at home this season after going 12-29 last campaign at Barclays Center.


              Orlando appeared to have the game under control after Jalen Suggs hit a 3-pointer for a 106-104 lead with 3:22 remaining.


              On the next possession, the Nets used one of their challenges that overturned an offensive foul on Mikel Brown Jr. He was credited with a basket and was awarded a free throw that evened the game at 106.


              Randle later hit a jumper and Bane answered with a 3 that made it 109-109. Randle then converted a pair of free throws before Wendell Carter Jr. tied the game with a putback layup with 31 seconds left following Franz Wagner’s errant 3-pointer before he made up for it before time expired.


              Up next
              Magic: At Washington on Sunday.


              Nets: At Minnesota on Monday.

articles.headline: Davis and Dybantsa help the Wizards knock off the Bulls 98-94 in NBA Cup action
articles.description: — Anthony Davis had 36 points and 11 rebounds, and the Washington Wizards beat the Chicago Bulls 98-94 in an NBA Cup game on Friday night.
articles.body:
CHICAGO -- — Anthony Davis had 36 points and 11 rebounds, and the Washington Wizards beat the Chicago Bulls 98-94 in an NBA Cup game on Friday night.


              AJ Dybantsa had 20 points, 10 rebounds and six assists for Washington, which posted its second straight win after an eight-game losing streak. Trae Young scored 16 points, and Kyshawn George finished with 11.


              The Wizards grabbed control with a 12-0 run in the fourth quarter, highlighted by a reverse jam by Dybantsa in transition. The No. 1 pick in this year's draft capped the spurt with a layup that made it 89-78 with 7:31 left.


              Chicago closed to 96-94 on Nic Claxton's two free throws with 43 seconds left. Norman Powell had a chance to tie the game in the final seconds, but he missed a floater and Young made two foul shots at the other end. 


              Powell scored 16 points for Chicago, and Buddy Hield had 15. The Bulls, who lost 124-120 to Washington in their home opener on Oct. 24, led by as many as 15 in the first half.


              The Bulls dropped to 1-2 in NBA Cup action. The Wizards are 2-1 with one game left in group play.


              Washington opened the third quarter with a 15-2 run, taking a 67-62 lead on Davis' layup with 5:56 left. Young made a go-ahead 3-pointer during the stretch.


              The Wizards carried a 75-69 lead into the final period after outscoring the Bulls 23-9 in the third. The Wizards also controlled the third in the first meeting of the season, outscoring the Bulls 40-20 in the quarter.


              Chicago played without rookie Caleb Wilson, who missed his fifth straight game. The 6-foot-10 forward had surgery on his right hand on Nov. 12.


              Up next
              Wizards: Host the Orlando Magic on Sunday night.


              Bulls: Host the Denver Nuggets on Sunday night.

articles.headline: Fantasy football Week 11 inactives: Who's in and who's out?
articles.description: Updated inactives and analysis based on the latest reports and official announcements leading up to kickoff.
articles.body:
Biggest injury concerns for Week 11

Players with early starts

Carson Beck, QB, Cardinals (back): Beck popped up on Thursday's injury report with a back injury. He has dealt with this issue throughout the season and currently appears to be unlikely to play in Week 11. Josh Johnson would be next man up and is purely a two-QB format option for those who are desperately in need of a bye week/injury replacement. In either event, Trey McBride is the only Cardinals player who should be started with any confidence -- and even his value is diminished in this new-look Cardinals offense.

Dalton Kincaid, TE, Bills (thumb/ankle): Kincaid has not yet practiced this week and is doubtful for Week 11. With the Bills playing the Chiefs on Thanksgiving -- just four days after this game -- expect Buffalo to use caution here. If he sits, Dawson Knox becomes a deeper streaming option against a Dolphins team that has allowed the fifth-most TE fantasy PPG.

Don't forget to check these out: Mike Clay's Playbook | Week 11 Buzz 

Week 11 Rankings | Matchup rankings for Week 11

Official Sunday inactives should begin coming in approximately 90 minutes before the scheduled kickoff times: around 11:30 a.m. ET for the early games and 2:30 p.m. ET for the late-afternoon games.

Refresh often for the latest information.

Jonathon Brooks, RB, Panthers (groin): Brooks is questionable for Week 11 but seems close to making his return after having practiced in full all week. He is worth adding if he is available on your league's waiver wire, but fantasy managers should take a wait-and-see approach. Chuba Hubbard remains an RB1 play.

Darren Waller, TE, Panthers (knee): Waller is questionable for Week 11 after limited practices Thursday and Friday. Waller is a TD-dependent streaming option. Some preferred TE plays are Mark Andrews and Chig Okonkwo. Waller should be used over Brenton Strange, Dallas Goedert and Mike Gesicki.

Kyle Monangai, RB, Bears (toe): Monangai is off the injury report, meaning he will play in week 11. He has not played since Week 4. Still, he is in the mix as a flex option due to a matchup against the Saints. New Orleans has allowed the fourth-most rushing yards to RBs, as well as the second-most RB fantasy points.

Caleb Douglas, WR, Dolphins (shoulder): Douglas had been limited at practice this week before elevating to full on Friday. He is off the injury report, meaning he will play in Week 11. Jordyn Tyson, WR, Saints (chest): Tyson has been limited at practice this week and is questionable for Week 11. If he plays, he'd be a WR3 (with a lot more upside). articles.headline: Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane out a 'few months' after ankle injury
articles.description: Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane is set to be out for several months after suffering a ligament tear in his left ankle during Bayern Munich's draw with Cologne.
articles.headlineJa: バロンドール受賞者のハリー・ケイン、足首の負傷で「数ヶ月」離脱へ
articles.descriptionJa: バロンドール受賞者のハリー・ケインが、バイエルン・ミュンヘン対ケルンの引き分け試合中に左足首の靭帯断裂を負い、数ヶ月の間離脱することが決まった。
articles.body:
Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane is set to be sidelined for several months after suffering a ligament tear in his left ankle in the first half of Bayern Munich's draw at home to FC Cologne in the Bundesliga on Friday.

Kane was hurt while attempting to get on the end of a deflected Olise cross in front of goal, when Cologne defender Joel Schmied got to the ball first and clattered into Kane's left leg in his follow through.

Bayern subsequently confirmed that Kane had been diagnosed with a ligament tear following an examination, adding that the England international would be out "for the next few months."

Bayer sporting director Max Eberl said they expected Kane to miss around three months.

Kane immediately clutched his lower leg after the injury and writhed in pain for a few moments before gingerly getting back to his feet, but he was a virtual bystander for the next couple of minutes.

The 33-year-old gestured to the sideline, sunk to the turf and then received treatment on his ankle before making way for Tom Bischof in the 20th minute, limping off the field alongside two physios.

Kane last month was announced as the men's Ballon d'Or winner after a prolific year with Bayern and England. He is Bayern's first winner of the prestigious award in 45 years and the first English winner in 25 years.

His injury means he is almost certain to miss Bayern's remaining four games in the Champions League league phase and could be in jeopardy for the start of the knockout phase, which begins in February, if Bayern progress.

England will hope that Kane has returned in time for their UEFA Nations League quarterfinal with Norway at the end of March.

Cologne were leading 1-0 at the time of Kane's injury through a 12th-minute goal from Mikey Moore before Nathaniel Brown equalized in the 37th minute.

However, Michael Olise added to Bayern's injury woes as he was substituted at the start of the second half, having hobbled off just before the break following a collision with Tom Krauss.

Olise later left the stadium on crutches, though coach Vincent Kompany said that was a precautionary measure. Bayern said that Olise had a bruised forefoot and would receive treatment in the coming days.

Any prolonged absence for Kane and Olise would be a major blow to Bayern. The pair account for 22 for Bayern's 54 goals (41%) this season.

Despite dominating possession against Cologne, Bayern had only one shot on goal over the 90 minutes as they failed to find a winner. It was the first time Bayern Munich had just one shot on target in a Bundesliga home game since at least 2004-05.

The game was Bayern's first since the November international break, in which Kane scored in England's Nations League wins over Spain and Croatia and became England's record appearance maker.

articles.headline: Back at practice again, Bengals QB Burrow optimistic he'll be at full strength
articles.description: A full participant at practice for the second straight day despite the bug that he has battled, Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow is optimistic that he'll be at full strength when Cincinnati plays the Washington Commanders on "Monday Night Football."
articles.body:
CINCINNATI -- With hushed tones and a plaid orange-and-black beanie nearly pulled over his eyes, Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow was limited in his comments about the illness ailing him ahead of Monday's game against the Washington Commanders.

But importantly, Burrow was optimistic that he'll be at full strength when Cincinnati plays in its second primetime game and third showcase game in as many weeks.

"Getting better," Burrow said after Friday's practice.

The injury report confirmed Burrow's comments, too. He was a full participant for the second straight day despite the bug that he has battled in recent days.

Typically, Burrow talks to reporters following the first practice of the game week. But given his condition, the team bumped him an extra day as he tries to recover.

Wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase took his place instead and had a little fun with the switch. He wore Burrow's practice jersey to his news conference, opened with Burrow's trademark greeting (either one or two "hellos") and even answered a couple of questions as if he was Burrow.

But when it came time to get serious, Chase felt like Burrow was still in good shape.

"Overall, he looks good," Chase said Thursday. "I think everybody around the team is coming down with a little sickness. But overall, he still looks good, still feels the same."

Various members of the team have felt ill in recent days, starting with right guard Dalton Risner, who was added to the injury report shortly before the team's 38-18 win against the Pittsburgh Steelers last Sunday night. Risner eventually left the game because of knee injuries and has not practiced yet this week.

Burrow isn't the only starter this week who is under the weather. Cornerback Dax Hill missed his second straight practice as he also battles an illness. Myles Hinton, a backup tackle, returned to practice after being sick on Thursday.

Burrow's proven strategy to get better: sleep, hydrate and eat spicy foods.

And it helps that Cincinnati (7-2) has an extra day to prepare for the Commanders (3-5-1) given how the players have felt physically.

"A lot of sick guys early in the week, so I don't know if the energy would've been there if we were a Sunday game coming in on Wednesday," Burrow said. "But we had three days off. It was a little lower yesterday, guys coming off of that, but today guys got after it and we're ready to go."

The "Monday Night Football" contest will also mark Burrow's first regular-season game at Washington since 2020, since he suffered a season-ending ACL injury in his rookie season, an event that feels like a lifetime ago.

"It's been a long time," Burrow said. "It is crazy. This season has gone by quickly and the last six years have gone by very quickly. A lot has happened for sure."

articles.headline: NFL Week 11 uniforms: Texans debut Rivalries look, Commanders rock 'Hail Raiser'
articles.description: Here's a look at what each NFL team is wearing in Week 11, led by Houston debuting its Rivalries combination.
articles.headlineJa: NFL第11週のユニフォーム：テキサンズが「ライバルズ」仕様を初披露、コマンダーズは「ヘイル・レイザー」を着用
articles.descriptionJa: ヒューストンが初披露する「ライバルズ」コンビネーションをはじめ、NFL各チームが第11週に着用するユニフォームを紹介する。
articles.body:
A primetime game can be a perfect opportunity for a team to send a message with its play. It also helps when it is looking its finest on the gridiron. The Houston Texans and Washington Commanders enter Week 10 with one part of that down with the debut of their respective uniforms.

It was the Texans' turn first, as they wore their Rivalries threads against the Indianapolis Colts on "Thursday Night Football." The look is primarily white, but includes H-Town blue and battle red with details that pay homage to Houston's streets. The city's signature blue street tiles appear on the uniform's helmet, name plate, sleeve, collar and pant stripes in a two-tone battle red and blue finish. Houston's "be someone" bridge is the inspiration for the blue jersey numbers.

For the first time, the Texans wore a liberty white helmet, paying tribute to the white prototype founder Robert C. McNair revealed in 1999 before shifting to a deep steel blue lid. The white helmet's face mask includes a chrome H-town blue finish, a nod to Houston's car culture. 

As part of the Commanders' redesign of their uniform closet last offseason, they unveiled the all-black "Hail Raiser" alternates, which debut against the Cincinnati Bengals on "Monday Night Football." It features a black helmet with a "Spear W" logo on both sides, as the spear and "W" are interwoven at their center. Burgundy and gold stripes appear on the sleeve and pants, while the lid includes a three-stripe look on top of similar colors. Solid burgundy block numbers are outlined by gold. 

The Buffalo Bills are also rocking a Rivalries look against the Miami Dolphins. Buffalo debuted its all-white "Cold Front" combination last season, but it returns with icy details throughout. The shoulder sleeve features a chrome charging buffalo, the first time a Bills uniform incorporates this element. The white helmet similarly includes a frosty metallic-filled charging buffalo logo, while the shoulder and pant leg patters boast a cracked-ice texture with a pattern that resembles snowfall on a bison's fur. 

It's an alternate week for the Detroit Lions as well. Detroit is going all-black against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Complete with a Honolulu blue matte helmet, the "Motor City Muscle" threads were first unveiled in 2024. The lid also includes a leaping lion logo in silver with a black stripe down the middle. The Lions wore these threads in Week 7 against the Green Bay Packers.

articles.headline: Sources: Tom Brady buys stake in Chelsea after Birmingham exit
articles.description: Seven-time Super Bowl champion quarterback Tom Brady has invested in Chelsea soccer club, sources confirmed to ESPN and NFL Network.
articles.headlineJa: 【関係者】トム・ブレイディ、バーミンガム離脱後にチェルシーの株式を取得
articles.descriptionJa: スーパーボウルで7度の優勝経験を持つクォーターバックのトム・ブレイディが、サッカークラブのチェルシーに投資したことが、ESPNとNFLネットワークへの情報筋により確認された。
articles.body:
Seven-time Super Bowl champion quarterback Tom Brady has purchased a stake in Chelsea soccer club, sources confirmed to ESPN and NFL Network. 

The deal would make the NFL legend a minority investor in the Clearlake Capital vehicle that controls Chelsea, sources close to global investment firm added to ESPN. Brady is expected to serve as an operating adviser to Clearlake but would not have voting rights with the club.

Brady left the ownership group of second-tier English club Birmingham City earlier this month after becoming a minority owner with a 3.3% stake.

Defense attorney Alex Spiro is part of Brady's ownership group and helped negotiate the deal. 

Brady had also held a position on the club's advisory board via a partnership with Birmingham's owner, Knighthead Capital Management, headed by his friend and business partner Tom Wagner.

Todd Boehly and fellow co-owner Mark Walter sold their stakes in Chelsea this past September in a deal that gives Clearlake Capital full control of the English Premier League club.

Private equity firm Clearlake, led by Behdad Eghbali and Jose E. Feliciano, previously owned a 61.5% stake in Chelsea, while U.S. businessmen Walter and Boehly each owned 12.83%. Swiss philanthropist Hansjörg Wyss, who also owned a 12.83% stake, remains a partner in the ownership group.

The consortium bought Chelsea for £2.5 billion ($3.3 billion) in 2022 with a further £1.75 billion ($2.3 billion) committed to investment in the club after former owner Roman Abramovich was sanctioned because of alleged ties to Russian President Vladimir Putin following the country's invasion of Ukraine.

The Financial Times reported that Walter and Boehly will receive £950 million ($1.3 billion) for their combined stake in a deal that values the club at £5 billion ($6.7 billion) including debt.

Neither Chelsea nor Clearlake Capital has replied to ESPN's request for comment about Brady's purchase of shares. 

Brady purchased a 5% minority stake in the Las Vegas Raiders in 2024 after NFL owners unanimously approved the deal. 

ESPN's Adam Schefter and James Olley as well as NFL Network's Ian Rapoport contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Raiders TE Brock Bowers (ankle, quad) listed as questionable
articles.description: Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers (ankle/quad) is questionable for Sunday's divisional matchup against the Denver Broncos, coach Klint Kubiak said Friday.
articles.headlineJa: レイダースのTEブロック・バワーズ（足首、大腿四頭筋）は出場が不透明
articles.descriptionJa: クリント・クビアック監督は金曜日、ラスベガス・レイダースのタイトエンドであるブロック・バワーズ（足首、大腿四頭筋）について、日曜日のデンバー・ブロンコスとの地区対決への出場が不透明であると語りました。
articles.body:
HENDERSON, Nev. -- Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers (ankle/quad) is questionable for Sunday's divisional matchup against the Denver Broncos, coach Klint Kubiak said Friday.

Bowers practiced for two straight days after not participating Wednesday and said he's "feeling all right."

Kubiak didn't say whether Bowers will work out pregame to determine his game status. When Bowers was asked if he felt optimistic about his availability for the Week 11 contest with playoff implications, he said: "We'll see."

"I don't know. We still have some conversations to have," Bowers added.

Bowers injured his right ankle on the opening drive of the Raiders' 21-13 loss to the Seattle Seahawks. At the 11:31 mark, left tackle Kolton Miller and a Seahawks defender tumbled over Bowers' leg during an Ashton Jeanty rushing attempt. Bowers remained on the ground before walking off the field under his own power.

Bowers went into the medical tent and then returned to the field for Fernando Mendoza's 10-yard touchdown run. Bowers headed to the locker room after that play and was listed as questionable to return by the team.

He returned with 13:30 to go in the second quarter and made a 12-yard reception on third down. Later in the quarter, Bowers went back to the locker room, where he stayed for the rest of the first half before ultimately being ruled out.

Bowers finished with two catches for 18 yards, upping his season totals to 50 catches for 676 yards and six touchdowns. The Raiders' offense collapsed in his absence, totaling just 27 net yards in the second half.

"I really wanted to play, so I was just doing everything I could to get back out there, like just trying a new tape job and stuff," Bowers said while reflecting on last week's game. "Felt it each time I went back out there. It was tough."

The Raiders also face a kicker dilemma. Matt Gay (hip) is questionable to play. Gay didn't practice Thursday but was on the field Wednesday and Friday, and Kubiak said he practiced well.

With uncertainty surrounding Gay's injury, the Raiders worked out three kickers Thursday: Lucas Havrisik, Younghoe Koo and John Parker Romo. If needed, the Raiders could elevate practice squad kicker and undrafted rookie Kansei Matsuzawa.

"We have Plan B and a Plan C. We got Special K [Matsuzawa]," Kubiak said.

articles.description: Real Madrid are looking to boost their attack by signing Como and Argentina international Nico Paz. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.headlineJa: 移籍の噂・ニュース：レアル・マドリード、来夏にコモのニコ・パス獲得の見込み
articles.descriptionJa: レアル・マドリードは、コモに所属するアルゼンチン代表のニコ・パスを獲得することで攻撃陣の強化を図っています。移籍情報の最新情報をお届けします。
articles.body:
Real Madrid are expected to trigger the €80 million release clause in Nico Paz's contract at Como next summer, while Athletic Club winger Nico Williams is back on the radar of Arsenal, among a host of others. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Real Madrid are expected to trigger the €80m release clause in Nico Paz's contract at Como, following another impressive campaign in Italy. Mundo Deportivo claims that Los Blancos have until next summer to activate the clause after recent uncertainty over his future. The 22-year-old playmaker first joined Como for €6m in 2024, but a restructured €60 million deal was reached last summer that increased his release clause. Paz has scored six goals and assisted eight in 14 appearances across all competitions, giving Real Madrid a huge decision to make over his future in the coming months.

- Arsenal have reignited their interest in Athletic Club winger Nico Williams, reports TEAMtalk. The Gunners have been heavily linked with the Spain World Cup winner in the past, but after he signed a new 10-year contract extension last summer, the prospects of a deal seemingly diminished, even with a €100m exit clause inserted in the agreement. Williams is now open to a move, while Arsenal are considering options for their left flank. Real Madrid's Endrick, RB Leipzig's Antonio Nusa, Brentford's Kevin Schade and Atlético Madrid forward Álex Baena are others being considered by the Premier League champions.

- Alejandro Balde continues to be linked with an exit from Barcelona, with his representatives exploring potential destinations for the left back this winter. Marca reports that the 23-year-old could make a move, with the Blaugrana keen to secure a permanent transfer rather than a loan. Any deal could be placed at roughly €40m, with Manchester United and Liverpool regularly linked.

- Aston Villa striker Tammy Abraham has emerged as an option for Valencia, according to Matteo Moretto, with contact already made. The 29-year-old has started just once under Unai Emery this campaign, which came in the EFL Cup. With a potential exit on the cards, Valencia have asked about a loan in January, with part of his salary covered.

- Napoli will let star midfielder Kevin De Bruyne leave the club in the January transfer window, if an offer of €7m arrives. Gazzetta dello Sport reports that the 35-year-old is wanted by PSV Eindhoven, which would move him closer to his native Belgium. Napoli chiefs are not keen on his exit, but will accept a move if any cost is recouped during the final six months of his contract.

- Chelsea have made an approach for Real Betis youngster José Antonio Morante, 19, after a breakout start to the campaign. The winger is also being tracked by Manchester City and Manchester United. (TEAMtalk)

articles.headline: Jets QB Geno Smith (ankle) cleared to start vs. Chargers
articles.description: Jets quarterback Geno Smith made it through the practice week with no setbacks and was cleared to face the Chargers.
articles.headlineJa: ジェッツのQBジーノ・スミス（足首）、チャージャーズ戦の先発出場が決定
articles.descriptionJa: ジェッツのクォーターバック、ジーノ・スミスは今週の練習を問題なく消化し、チャージャーズ戦への出場許可が下りました。
articles.body:
New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith, who said Wednesday that his plan is to play Sunday despite a balky left ankle, made it through the practice week with no setbacks and was cleared to face the Los Angeles Chargers.

After two days of limited practice, Smith was a full participant Friday and has no injury designation on the final report.

Before Friday's practice, coach Aaron Glenn said that Smith had looked "solid" on Wednesday and Thursday and that his prospects for playing were "very encouraging."

Smith injured his ankle in the third quarter of last Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Buffalo Bills. He underwent X-rays at the stadium and an MRI exam Monday, which showed no significant injury, a source said.

He was seen walking with a limp Wednesday, but Smith stated matter-of-factly that he intended to play. The spiraling Jets (2-8) have lost five in a row.

Some media members and fans are calling for rookie Cade Klubnik, who replaced Smith last Sunday, but Glenn has made it clear that Smith is the undisputed starter. Glenn said that Smith is performing well and that it would be "disrespectful" to replace him for the sake of evaluating Klubnik, a fourth-round pick from Clemson.

The Jets hope Smith can lead the offense out of its funk -- nine straight quarters without a touchdown. They will be without their No. 3 and No. 4 receivers: rookie Omar Cooper Jr (ankle, hip) and Isaiah Williams (ribs).

Tim Patrick, a healthy scratch last week, could be in the No. 3 role against the Chargers. They also could elevate veteran Sterling Shepard from the practice squad.

articles.headline: Drake Maye ankle injury: Is the Patriots' season over? Can Tommy DeVito step up?
articles.description: If the QB doesn't return in 2026, New England faces an uphill battle against some of the NFL's best teams.
articles.headlineJa: ドレイク・メイの足首の怪我：ペイトリオッツのシーズンは終わってしまうのか？トミー・デヴィートは期待に応えられるか？
articles.descriptionJa: もしこのQBが2026年に復帰できない場合、ニューイングランドはNFLの強豪チームを相手に厳しい戦いを強いられることになります。
articles.body:
The outlook for the New England Patriots' 2026 season has been dramatically altered. After suffering an injury on the Patriots' first drive against the Detroit Lions on Sunday, quarterback Drake Maye did not fly back from Munich with the team out of caution. Sources have told ESPN, Maye fractured his right fibula -- an injury that won't require surgery but is expected to sideline him deep into the regular season, if he is able to return this year at all.

The 5-5 Patriots haven't been among the AFC's elite in 2026, but were hoping to make a charge to the playoffs -- and Maye potentially finding his past runner-up MVP form was one of their silver linings.

When Maye was taking care of the football and extending plays, the Patriots were explosive and flashed potential to hang with the best -- as a Week 4 win at the Buffalo Bills showed. But when Maye was not buttoned-up with his decision-making (he entered Sunday with 11 INTs) the Patriots struggled. When he was cleaner in that area, it was just enough to get by some of the league's lower-echelon teams, with close wins against the New York Jets and Miami Dolphins, who have won a combined three games this season.

Coach Mike Vrabel often says it's hard to win when a team's best players don't play well, and simply put, Maye is the team's best offensive player.

Entering Week 10, he ranked top five in the NFL in Total QBR (74.2), passing touchdowns (18), yards per attempt (8.4), rushing yards by a quarterback (219) and rushing touchdowns by a quarterback (3).

Now potentially without Maye for weeks or even the season, the question is can the team make it back to the playoffs?

ESPN Patriots reporter Mike Reiss answers some of the top questions about the trickle-down effect of Maye's injury and analyst Matt Bowen answers a fantasy question on what to expect if you have Patriots players in your lineup.

Is the Patriots' 2026 season over?

When Vrabel was hired as head coach in January 2025, he said the team's goals were to win the division, host home playoff games and compete for championships. Their odds of doing that without Maye are closer to zero, starting with the current standings -- they are 5-5 while the AFC East rival Bills are 8-1.

Here is the rest of the Patriots' schedule: they are on the bye in Week 11 before a road trip to face the winless Los Angeles Chargers, then two huge home games in a span of five days -- vs. the Bills (Dec. 6) and the Minnesota Vikings (Dec. 10). Then they're at the Kansas City Chiefs and the New York Jets before finishing the year with home games against the Denver Broncos and the Miami Dolphins.

They have played poorly the past two weeks in blowout losses to the Packers and Lions, ravaged by injuries across the roster, but Maye's presence -- even as he battled through inconsistent play with turnovers -- gave them a sliver of hope.

articles.headline: Xabi Alonso: João Pedro still not available, whole team needs to step up
articles.description: Xabi Alonso said his Chelsea side need to learn to deal with the absence of João Pedro as the Blues struggle for goals in the absence of their injured striker.
articles.body:
Xabi Alonso said his Chelsea side need to learn to deal with the absence of João Pedro as the Blues struggle for goals in the absence of their injured striker.

The Brazilian has not played since the 2-0 win over Everton on Oct. 17 and will be unavailable again when Leeds visit Stamford Bride on Saturday.

He was a key part of Chelsea's explosive attacking start to the campaign. With five goals he is joint-second top scorer this season, but in his absence the side have posed a far less potent forward threat.

They have scored only one Premier League goal from open play in the four games Pedro has missed, while without him both Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers have found it harder to influence matches.

Without a focal point in the number nine position, Palmer and Rogers have found linking up together more difficult and Chelsea's goal output has been dramatically reduced.

With the Blues having dropped to fifth and having suffered two defeats in their last three games, including an especially insipid 1-0 loss to Sunderland who were bottom of the league at the time, Alonso insisted they cannot simply wait for their striker to regain fitness.

"[We need] the whole team for that," Alonso said. "It's not just the strikers that can score. We can score from set-pieces, from defenders, from midfielders.

"It's teamwork. For sure Joao is an important player but we need to deal with this time without him. So far we have tried different options and we need to keep trying.

"We need to deal with it. It's not that I'm going to look for one explanation. I think that there are more explanations for one defeat than missing just one player.

"If we do more things right, we could compete better and win at Sunderland, but there are a few things that had to be done. We want Joao Pedro back but I don't want to make a big thing out of that."

Alonso is not without options in the striker position. Danny Welbeck and summer signing Emmanuel Emegha can both play as like-for-like replacements while Rogers and Pedro Neto have also been experimented with as false number nines.

"[Emegha and Welbeck] are both ready, both different qualities, different stages of their career," Alonso said. "Danny had played so many games, he has great experience. Ema, he has this power, this physicality, he's waiting for a chance. We have enough games for him."

Welbeck, who is 35 and joined from Brighton in the summer, has scored three times this season, all in the Carabao Cup, while Emegha, a summer buy from Strasbourg, is yet to open his account having only made his debut in October following injury.

articles.headline: Pochettino: 'Massive' pressure with USMNT makes me better coach for Man United
articles.description: Mauricio Pochettino said the experience of coaching the U.S. at the World Cup stands him in good stead for taking over Manchester United.
articles.body:
Pressure? What pressure?

Mauricio Pochettino said the experience of coaching the United States at the World Cup stands him in good stead for taking over Manchester United and trying to resurrect one of soccer's fallen giants.

Pochettino left his role with the U.S. this week to take over a United that has not won the Premier League in 13 years and sits in the relegation zone after its worst start in 40 years.

- Pochettino wants input on Man United transfer decisions

- Ex-U.S. coach Arena: Federation doesn't 'have a clue' how to replace Poch

- Pochettino's Man United squad audit: Big calls to make on stars like Fernandes, Rashford

On Friday, he said his time in America means he arrives at Old Trafford at the height of his powers.

"We are much better coaches now after work in the national team like USA because the expectation and the pressure was massive," the Argentine said. "I remember in SoFi [Stadium in California], our first [World Cup] game against Paraguay, the pressure was massive. There was more than 200 celebrity people expecting us to win and to play well and all the country was behind us.

"When you are in the Premier League or in LaLiga or in France, OK, you feel the pressure when you manage these types of clubs, but being there, I promise, was massive pressure."

Pochettino teared up when he farewelled the U.S. program but on Friday he looked in his element at his first news conference in Manchester after two days working with the team.

The former Tottenham, Paris Saint-Germain and Chelsea manager said he'd missed the day-to-day rhythm of club soccer.

"We were missing a lot," he said.

"I think we are animals of the grass. We like to feel the grass. We need to smell the grass and try to help the players to improve every day. It's true that it's a different job when you are in the national team, but in the same time you learn a lot and I think we are much better coaches now."

Pochettino takes over a club in crisis, on a run of one win in 10 games. United was 18th in the standings and things could get worse with a daunting trip to Liverpool on Sunday.

"It's a race to arrive in condition to be competitive against Liverpool," Pochettino said. "We arrived with the idea to create something from scratch, from our own ideas and philosophy in the way that we love to work.

"What we need to do is to be very open-minded ... the players need to buy the idea of what we need to improve. After a few days working the job is to try to find a way from Sunday to perform and to start to get the results that the club historically needs.

"Manchester United need to be in a different place than we are now."

Pochettino led the U.S. men's national team to an 8-0 aggregate win over Haiti in the Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals earlier this week in the final act of his two-year stint as coach.

articles.headline: Champions League upstarts Como suffer Moise Kean injury blow
articles.description: Como forward Moise Kean is set to be out injured for at least two months and could miss Champions League games against Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona.
articles.body:
Como forward Moise Kean is set to be out injured for at least two months, his coach Cesc Fabregas said on Friday, and could miss Champions League games against Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona.

The 26-year-old Italy forward injured his right leg against Belgium in the Nations League this week but the latest issue was with his left leg, Fabregas said.

- Meet Como's Nico Paz, the heir to Lionel Messi's No. 10 shirt for Argentina

- UCL talking points: First upsetting United, now NINE goals!? Are Como the real deal?

Como previously said Kean needed treatment on an injury in practice after returning from national team duty.

In its first season in the Champions League, Como have adapted stunningly fast with a 9-1 win at Lens and a pair of 4-1 victories at home to Manchester United and RB Leipzig.

Como are fourth in the 36-team standings ahead of hosting AEK Athens on Tuesday. The league phase for Como finishes with Real Betis next month and titleholders PSG, one of Kean's former clubs, and Barcelona in back-to-back weeks in January.

Kean arrived at Como on an initial season-long loan from Fiorentina and his injury leaves just Tasos Douvikas as a proven striker until the January transfer window. Kean has been limited to just four appearances for Como so far this season.

Como are fifth in Serie A and host Cagliari on Saturday.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.
